problems.title: Token normalization does not sample the general sequence-level target
problems.source_location: Eq.(8), PDF p.5; Algorithm 1 lines 9–11 and target interpretation, p.6
claim: The paper defines \(p_T(x)\propto p_D(x)^R q(x)^{1-R}\), but normalizes mixed logits separately at each token.
analysis: Take two binary positions, uniform factorized \(p_D=1/4\), \(R=1/2\), and verifier joint \(q=(0.49,0.01,0.25,0.25)\) over \(00,01,10,11\). Global normalization gives \(p_T=(7/18,1/18,5/18,5/18)\), first-token probability \(4/9\). Local normalization keeps first token uniform and yields joint \((7/16,1/16,1/4,1/4)\), with total variation \(1/18\). All probabilities are positive. Here identical first-token shared-randomness draws make the draft and sampled target prefix agree, avoiding a separate draft-prefix approximation. In general local denominators depend on the path; one global partition function cannot replace their product.
result: The general target-draw identification is false. Endpoint \(R=0,1\), history-independent conditionals or constant normalizer products are special controls. Eq.(8) is a valid distribution definition, and the final adaptive output was not established to be promised equal to it.
repair: Explicitly define the local verifier distributions and scope the acceptance rule accordingly. Exact global-target conditionals would require suffix partition sums, for which no efficient implementation is established.

problems.title: The positive-temperature helper effectively squares temperature
problems.source_location: Appendix C, PDF p.14; generation_utils.py, lines 97–123
claim: The sampler divides logits by \(T\), then divides exponentiated scores by \(E^T\), with \(E=-\log U\).
analysis: The maximizing score is equivalent to \(\ell/T^2-\log E\), hence its retained-support law is softmax at \(T^2\). Filtering first uses \(T\), so with active cutoffs the whole sampler is not simply a conventional \(T^2\) sampler. For logits \((0,0.2)\), \(T=0.2\), top-p \(0.95\), both tokens survive filtering. Nominal second-token probability is \(e/(1+e)=0.7310585786\), versus implemented \(e^5/(1+e^5)=0.9933071491\). At \(T=1\) the discrepancy disappears; the zero-temperature greedy branch is separate.
result: The supported positive-temperature path uses a different law from its nominal setting and the repository’s ordinary categorical baseline. Benchmark direction/magnitude and historical use remain unestablished.
repair: Apply temperature once, filter the intended logits, then add standard Gumbel noise: \(X=\arg\max[\operatorname{filter}(\ell/T)+G]\). Preserve a common explicit filtering/sampling convention when comparing methods.

problems.title: The target call ignores the supplied shared randomness
problems.source_location: Algorithm 1 and one-shot endpoint, PDF p.6; generation_utils.py, apd_accept_criterion lines 126–138
claim: The target sampler call passes noise but omits temperature; its zero default returns raw logits and ignores noise.
analysis: Use two positions with logits \((0,0.2)\), \(T=0.2,R=1\), top-p \(0.95\), positive noise factors \((0.3,0.9)\). Proposal scores are \(1/0.3=3.3333\) and \(e/0.9=3.0203\), choosing token \(0\) at both positions. These factors have an open admissible neighborhood under the source noise transform. The target default chooses greedy token \(1\), and forced first acceptance yields mask \((1,0)\). Identical distributions evaluated with the same sampling map/noise must instead produce \((1,1)\).
result: The helper fails the stated shared-noise endpoint for supported stochastic proposals. Coincidental greedy agreement and zero-temperature proposals are countercontrols; no natural-prompt failure frequency is established.
repair: Use one canonical noise tensor and identical explicit temperature/filtering/tie conventions for both sampling paths. At the identical-distribution endpoint, equality then follows directly. This does not repair the separate global-target interpretation.
